textRuns.value: INSIGHT:
Cost and margin pressure (financial stress) shows an uneven distribution across facilities when viewed against an all-facilities median rather than within peer groups.
Variation in the cost-to-charge ratio remains clustered, with a subset of facilities positioned well above the system-wide reference line, while a broad middle and lower segment spans below it.

This indicates that financial stress exposure is concentrated in specific facilities rather than uniformly elevated across the system. Using a single, all-facilities median reframes relative positioning but does not change the underlying structural signal: pressure is unevenly distributed, not system-wide.
Overall, this pattern reflects distribution and concentration of financial stress exposure, not performance ranking, causality, or financial effectiveness.
INTERPRETATION GUIDELINES:
How to read this visual
Bars represent facility-level cost-to-charge ratios as a directional indicator of margin pressure.
The all-facilities median line provides a system-wide contextual benchmark, not a target or standard.
Distance above or below the median reflects relative exposure to financial stress within the system, not efficiency or management quality.
Ordering emphasizes spread and concentration, not priority or rank-based performance.
What this does not imply
This view does not control for peer-group differences, case mix, or market structure.
It does not establish causal reasons for higher or lower margin pressure.
It does not assign financial performance scores or judgments.
How to use this insight
Use this view to understand where financial stress is concentrated at the system level.
Compare this system-wide exposure lens with peer-group views to distinguish structural context from relative positioning.
Interpret downstream financial or operational metrics with this baseline context in mind, not as standalone evidence.
This visual should be used as a system-level baseline lens, not an explanatory endpoint.
